result.rule: When the description states one step in which the actor chooses or sets several attributes, joined by commas or 'and' in the same clause, and the attributes are listed as separate items: Name the task for that step so that its label includes every attribute the description lists for the step, using the description's own wording for each one. Do not shorten the label to only some of the listed attributes. Keep the label in the description's language and short.

When the description states, in one sentence, a step performed by an actor followed by further steps by the same actor (for example 'after doing X, the actor provides Y and Z', or 'the actor receives A and B'), so that one sentence contains an earlier action and one or more later actions joined by 'and' or commas: Model the earlier action and each later action as separate tasks, in the order the sentence gives them, and connect them in sequence. Also model each information item or sub-action named in an 'and'-joined list as its own task when the description treats it as a separate action. Name each task only after the act the description attributes to it, and do not let one task's label absorb the actions of another task.

When the description lists several kinds of items delivered to one recipient in a single clause, joined by commas and 'or', and each listed kind is a distinct communication: Model each listed kind of item as its own task, in the order the description gives them, instead of merging them into one task. Use the description's wording for each task label so that every kind keeps its own activity.

When the description states one actor performing several distinct activities in a single sentence, with the activities listed in a comma-separated or 'and'-joined series: Model each listed activity as its own task, in the order stated, and do not merge two or more of them into one task, even when they share an actor and a sentence. Keep them as separate tasks in sequence unless the description gives a dependency that requires a gateway.
